source.title: Are there topological versions of the idea of divisor?

accepted.question_text: In algebraic geometry, a divisor is described here as a formal integer linear combination of codimension-one subvarieties, while principal divisors and linear equivalence add analytic data through orders of vanishing and poles of functions along those subvarieties. Is there a purely topological construction, especially for non-smooth or non-manifold spaces, that similarly combines codimension-one cycle data with cohomological data from functions or function-like objects into a single fundamental group analogous to the divisor class group, with integer coefficients distinguished rather than arbitrary?
accepted.context_brief: Topological analogue of divisor class groups

evidence.quote: My question then is whether there exists a purely topological version of this subtle mixture of homology and cohomology.
